recent_articles.title: A.P. continues to grapple with intense heat as 95 mandals record above 42°C - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andhra Pradesh** continues to experience intense heat, with 95 out of 688 mandals recording temperatures above 42°C.  The highest temperature reached 45.8°C at Kanumolu in Krishna district. While some districts received light to moderate rainfall on Saturday, severe heatwave conditions are expected for 21 mandals and widespread heatwave conditions for 214 mandals on Sunday. The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts that weather systems brewing over the Bay of Bengal may bring isolated showers with lightning and thunderstorms in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema next week, but this activity is not expected to be widespread.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court declines to interfere with forest clearances for Adani’s Madhya Pradesh coal block project - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** declined to intervene in environmental clearances granted to the Adani Group's coal block project in Madhya Pradesh. The court noted a delay in challenging the approvals and observed that the National Green Tribunal (NGT) had relied on a 2025 ruling regarding limitation periods for challenges.  While the petitioner argued for judicial review of the clearances due to environmental concerns, the **Adani Group** urged dismissal of the plea. The court suggested Mr. Dubey pursue other legal remedies and granted him liberty to do so.

recent_articles.title: Police register FIR after viral video shows BJP worker’s kin firing into the air at wedding - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Police** in Raipur, Chhattisgarh registered an FIR on Tuesday after a viral video showed individuals firing guns at a wedding function. The **DD Nagar Police** stated that the incident violated firearm license conditions and could be considered negligence under various laws, including the BNS and Arms Act.  The video sparked outrage online and backlash from the Opposition.

recent_articles.title: Over ₹1 crore cash, AK-47 rifles recovered from Maoist hideouts, say police - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Police** in **Narayanpur district**, **Chhattisgarh**, have recovered over ₹1.01 crore in cash and a significant amount of arms and ammunition, including AK-47 and SLR rifles, from former Maoist hideouts or dumps in the past month.  The largest recovery was made on May 9th at Nelangur village near the Chhattisgarh-Maharashtra border, where ₹84 lakh in cash was found alongside two AK-47 rifles.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Police rescue 42 cattle, seize two vehicles in separate incidents in Peddapalli - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sultanabad police** rescued 42 bulls and cows from two separate vehicles in Peddapalli district on Sunday.  A Hyderabad-bound container lorry carrying 33 bulls was seized at a check post near Dubbapalli, while a van with 9 cows destined for an undisclosed location in Karnataka was intercepted at the same location. The police registered a case against the van's crew, Syed Shabad and Moiuddin, and transferred the rescued animals to a nearby goshala.

recent_articles.title: Punjab Congress to release ‘chargesheet’ against AAP government - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bhupesh Baghel**, former **Chhattisgarh** Chief Minister and Congress General Secretary in charge of Punjab, presided over a meeting of the state party unit to discuss the "grim state of affairs" under the ruling **AAP** government. The meeting focused on allegations of rampant corruption and deteriorating law and order, leading to feelings of insecurity among residents.  The **Congress** plans to hold "yatras" across all 117 Assembly segments in the coming days to engage with voters and address their concerns.

recent_articles.title: Two traffickers held - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bengaluru Rural police** intercepted a truck carrying 250 kg of ganja concealed in poultry feed, arresting two men, **Ramyan Yadav** and **Sabir Khan**, who were transporting the feed from Chhattisgarh to Tamil Nadu.  The investigation revealed that the men had been hired by a man from their native place to transport the contraband to a receiver in Bengaluru. The **Jigani police** have booked them under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, with further investigations ongoing.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: Independent journalism punished, compliance rewarded under current regime, says Kharge - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge** criticized the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** government for its alleged attempts to suppress press freedom in India.  He stated that since 2014, India's position in the World Press Freedom Index has declined and the BJP is seeking to tighten its control over social media to silence dissent. **Kharge** also accused the government of weaponizing legal frameworks to intimidate journalists and noted a sharp rise in arrests and imprisonments of journalists. He highlighted several high-profile cases, including those of journalists murdered while reporting on corruption.  He urged for upholding democratic norms by those in power.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh police personnel killed in IED blast during demining operation in Kanker - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chhattisgarh Police** officers were killed and one injured when an IED, previously planted by **Maoists**, detonated during a de-mining operation in Kanker district on Saturday.  The incident occurred as the team was defusing the device in a forest area under the Chhotebethiya police station.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh Assembly passes resolution for one-third quota for women in legislative bodies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Chhattisgarh Assembly** passed a resolution on Thursday calling for the immediate implementation of one-third reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures after delimitation. This follows the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which aimed to expedite women's reservation by redistributing Lok Sabha seats based on the 2011 Census.  The bill failed to secure a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha and since then, **BJP** governments have convened special sessions of state assemblies to push for its implementation.

recent_articles.title: Congress leader’s son shot dead, another son injured in Janjgir-Champa in Chhattisgarh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Unidentified assailants** barged into the home of **Congress leader Sammelal Kashyap** in Janjgir-Champa district, Chhattisgarh, on Friday (April 24, 2026), killing his son Aayush and injuring his younger son Ashutosh. The attackers arrived on a motorcycle and fired at the family while demanding money and mobile phones. **Congress State unit president Deepak Baij** condemned the incident as another example of deteriorating law and order in the state.

recent_articles.title: ED probes suspected TTI-linked funds routed through foreign bank debit cards - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Enforcement Directorate (ED)** conducted searches on April 18 and 19 at six locations in Assam, Chhattisgarh, and other places as part of an investigation into the suspected withdrawal and use of funds through foreign bank debit cards. The agency reported around ₹95 crore of inflow via such cards between November 2025 and April 2026, allegedly bypassing regulatory channels. This probe is linked to **The Timothy Initiative (TTI)** and associated persons under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).

recent_articles.title: Mahanadi tribunal gives last opportunity to Odisha, Chhattisgarh to settle river water dispute - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal (MWDT)**, chaired by former Supreme Court Judge Justice Bela M. Trivedi, is nearing a decision on the water sharing formula between **Odisha** and **Chhattisgarh**. The tribunal has given both states one last opportunity to finalize their proposals for mutual settlement by May 2, 2026, or face its own formulation.  The MWDT expressed dissatisfaction with the lack of concrete proposals and urged both parties to address the issues promptly.

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Government** celebrated National Panchayati Raj Day, highlighting the progress of women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).  While the Constitution mandates a 33% quota for women in urban and rural local bodies, 19 states have extended this provision to reserve 50% seats for women. However, data shows that the actual number of women representatives exceeds the prescribed quota in only 10 states/union territories, while four others fail to meet it.  The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.

recent_articles.title: Summer showers bring relief to residents in Kerala; heat, humid weather to continue - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Isolated spells of heavy rain** brought much-needed relief from the sweltering summer heat to parts of **Kerala** on Tuesday, with some areas experiencing rainfall exceeding 5 cm.  The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts isolated showers will continue for the next four days due to a trough/wind discontinuity running from North Chhattisgarh to the Comorin area. While these showers offer respite, the oppressive heat and humidity are expected to persist in most of the state, with temperatures exceeding 40°C in some areas.

recent_articles.title: Adani Power shares zoom nearly 40% in just 13 sessions. Should you book profits now? - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Adani Power**, India's largest private thermal power producer, is experiencing strong bullish momentum in its share price. The stock has recently broken out of a consolidation phase with expanding volumes and positive momentum across the **Adani Group**.  Traders are encouraged to hold existing long positions and view dips as buying opportunities. Analysts anticipate rising power demand due to the receding western disturbance that disrupted March's peak, which will benefit companies like **Adani Power** and NTPC.

recent_articles.title: SIR is a bloodless massacre, says Parakala Prabhakar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Parakala Prabhakar**, a political and economic analyst, criticized the proposed **Special Integrated Revision (SIR)** of electoral rolls in Telangana, calling it a "bloodless massacre" that threatens democratic rights. He questioned the need for a fresh revision when the annual Special Summary Revision (SSR) is already in place, criticizing the **Election Commission of India**'s justification and lack of transparency regarding irregularities and data released. Prabhakar cited examples from other states where SIR resulted in voter deletions with unclear criteria and inconsistencies, urging the government to first prepare the voter list through the State Election Commission before implementing SIR.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh Vedanta power plant blast: Death toll rises to 24 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A blast at the Vedanta power plant in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district has tragically claimed 24 lives, with one more fatality reported on Sunday.  **Vedanta Ltd.** workers were injured when a steel tube carrying high-pressure steam exploded, leaving several others critically burned. **Anil Agarwal**, chairman of **Vedanta Group**, and **Devendra Patel**, plant head, are among eight to ten individuals named in an FIR filed by police for causing death by negligence.  The incident is under investigation by both the police and state authorities.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh power plant explosion death toll touches 23 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vedanta** group chairman **Anil Agrawal** and others have been booked under BNS sections 106(1), 289, and 3(5) in connection with the explosion at a power plant in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district that killed 23 people.  The incident occurred on April 14, 2026, after an excessive accumulation of fuel inside the boiler furnace caused extreme pressure to build up, leading to the explosion of the tube connecting the boiler to the turbine. **Naveen Jindal**, industrialist and Lok Sabha MP, has come out in support of **Agrawal**, arguing that he had no role in the plant's operations and that the "Viksit Bharat" vision needs investors like him to keep investing and building.

recent_articles.title: Heatwave alert in Maharashtra till April 20; Akola hottest at 44.2°C - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** has issued heatwave alerts for six states, including Maharashtra, where temperatures are expected to rise by 1-2°C over the next three days. The highest recorded temperature in the country so far is 44.2°C in Akola district.  **Dr. Pradeep Awate**, former State Surveillance Officer, Maharashtra Health Services, attributes the rising temperatures to concrete projects and a decline in trees, which are contributing to increased heat in Mumbai. **Bikram Singh**, chief scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, stated that the IMD is vigilant and has already sent alerts regarding the heatwave conditions. The Maharashtra Government has implemented standard operating procedures (SOPs) to address the impact of the heatwaves, including regulating working hours during peak temperatures.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh power plant tragedy: toll rises to 21, Opposition wants culpable homicide charges to be slapped - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The death toll from this week's power plant explosion in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district has risen to 21, with another worker succumbing to his injuries on Thursday night.  **Vedanta Group** chairman **Anil Agrawal**, company manager **Devendra Patel**, and other responsible officers have been booked under BNS sections for prima facie negligence related to the accident. The **Congress** party is demanding charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder be added to the case, citing evidence suggesting inadequate maintenance and operation standards led to the boiler explosion.

recent_articles.title: Creeping risk: The Hindu Editorial on industrial accidents and neglect of risks - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Boiler explosions**, like the recent incident in Sakti, Chhattisgarh, are often caused by a gradual build-up of issues such as overpressure and scaling.  These incidents share similarities with other industrial disasters in India, including the Visakhapatnam gas leak and the Neyveli blast, highlighting systemic failures in boiler safety regulations. The current regulatory framework, which focuses on fabrication standards rather than continuous monitoring, has been criticized for failing to adequately address transient thermal and pressure imbalances that can lead to explosions.  The lack of surprise government inspections and a focus on "ease of doing business" have contributed to these issues, as evidenced by the exploitation of contract labor and inadequate safety measures in some facilities.

recent_articles.title: Billionaire Anil Agrawal named in Sakti power plant explosion FIR - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Vedanta group chairman Anil Agrawal** and others have been named in an FIR filed after a power plant blast in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district. The **Sakti Superintendent of Police Prafull Thakur** confirmed the charges, which include causing death by negligence, negligent conduct with respect to machinery, and common intention under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

recent_articles.title: Crushed dreams, close escapes, and questions of survival after a power plant tragedy - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A devastating explosion at **Vedanta’s** Singhitarai power plant in Chhattisgarh killed at least 20 people, including **Udhab Singh Yadav**, a farmer who had recently started working there for financial stability. The blast also claimed the lives of several other workers from different regions, leaving families grieving and facing financial hardship.  The tragedy has highlighted the precarious safety conditions at the plant, prompting concerns about worker compensation and potential negligence.

recent_articles.title: Watch: Delimitation controversy & Bihar’s first BJP CM | Above the Fold | 15.04.2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mallikarjun Kharge**, President of the **AICC** and Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha, announced that the **INDIA** bloc has unanimously decided to oppose the Delimitation Bill.  The death toll from the Sakti power plant explosion in Chhattisgarh rose to 16, while **Samrat Choudhary** was sworn in as Bihar's first BJP Chief Minister. Registration for the Amarnath Yatra is now open, starting July 3rd.
